_comment: One or two sentences per desktop app id (DESKTOP_APPS in lib/apps.js), read by tools/gen-site-pages.js for the per-app pages (apps/<id>.html). Only the desktop set gets a page; candidates, SDK samples and demos do not. Keep these factual: what the program is and, where known, how far it runs here.
_skip_comment: Desktop ids that get no page yet: they are not on the production desktop (wine-assembly.berrry.app/lib/apps.js) or have no usable screenshot. Remove an id from here, add its blurb, and shoot it with tools/screenshot-registry.sh when it ships.
_not_games_comment: Desktop ids outside the Win98 Accessories group that are not games: their page title says '<name> in your browser' rather than 'Play <name> in your browser'.
_titles_comment: Page name for an id whose short desktop label is not what people search for. Used in the title, H1, FAQ and JSON-LD; the desktop icon keeps its label.
notepad: The Windows 98 text editor, and the first program this emulator ever ran. Typing, selection, word wrap, Find and Replace, the Font and Open/Save dialogs and the help file all work.
calc: The Windows 98 Calculator in standard and scientific modes. It needs the real msvcrt.dll, which is loaded beside it.
mspaint98: Microsoft Paint from Windows 98: tool palette, colour box, zoom, text and the image menus, drawing into a real device-independent bitmap.
wordpad: WordPad from Windows 98, with its native RichEdit control, OLE embedding, print preview and the Word 6 and RTF file paths.
regedit: The Windows 98 Registry Editor, browsing the emulator's virtual registry through a tree view implemented in WAT.
taskman: The Windows 98 Task Manager, listing the windows the emulator has open.
sndrec32_98: Sound Recorder from Windows 98, recording and playing wave files through the emulated waveOut device.
freecell: FreeCell from the Windows 98 Entertainment Pack, using the real cards.dll. Fully playable with drag and drop.
sol: Solitaire from Windows 98, the Klondike game with cards.dll card faces. Fully playable, with scoring and timed games verified against the original.
cruel: Cruel, the Entertainment Pack solitaire variant where all cards are dealt face up.
golf: Golf solitaire from the Entertainment Pack: clear the columns onto the stock.
pegged: Pegged, the peg-solitaire board game from the Entertainment Pack.
snake: Rattler Race, the Entertainment Pack snake game. Steer with the arrow keys, start a level with F2.
wep16_rodent: Rodent's Revenge from Windows Entertainment Pack 2, the original 16-bit game: trap the cats with movable blocks. It runs through the NE loader, not a 32-bit port.
taipei: Taipei, the mahjong-solitaire tile game from the Entertainment Pack, with its 144-tile turtle layout.
tictac: TicTactics, the three-dimensional tic-tac-toe game from the Entertainment Pack.
reversi: Reversi from the Entertainment Pack: flip the computer's discs to your colour on the 8x8 board.
winmine_wep: Minesweeper, the Entertainment Pack build: clear the minefield from the numbered hints in beginner, intermediate or expert size.
ski32: SkiFree, the 32-bit port of the Entertainment Pack skiing game by Chris Pirih. Playable end to end, yeti included.
pinball: The Space Cadet pinball table that shipped with Windows XP, the original program: flippers, plunger, nudges, sound and high scores, tap-to-flip on phones.
spider: Spider Solitaire from Microsoft Plus! 98. Fully playable, including maximize.
marbles: Marbles from Microsoft Plus! 98, the first DirectDraw program the emulator rendered end to end.
bricks: Bricks, a community remake of the Klotski sliding-block puzzle.
empipe: EmPipe, a community remake of Pipe Dream.
funtris: Funtris, a community Tetris remake in the style of the Entertainment Pack original.
peaks: Peaks, a community remake of TriPeaks solitaire.
pyramid: Pyramid, a community remake of Tut's Tomb.
fourstones: FourStones, a community remake of Tic Tac Drop.
cwordzap: CWordZap, a community remake of WordZap.
dxball: DX-Ball, the freeware Breakout game by Michael P. Welch, running on DirectDraw. Shipped with the site as a freeware package.
blobby_volley: Blobby Volley, the freeware volleyball game where two blobs keep a ball off their side of the net, against a friend on the same keyboard or the computer.
winamp: Winamp 2.91, extracted from its installer. The skinned main window, playlist and equalizer draw through SetWindowRgn, and MP3 playback runs the real in_mp3 decoder on its own thread.
heroes2_demo: The Heroes of Might and Magic II demo from New World Computing: turn-based fantasy strategy with heroes, towns and tactical battles, shipped with the site.
rct: RollerCoaster Tycoon, Chris Sawyer's 1999 theme-park simulator written in assembly language: build coasters, run the park and keep the guests happy.
starcraft_shareware: Blizzard's 1998 StarCraft shareware demo, the real-time strategy game of Terrans, Zerg and Protoss. It opens on the first Terran mission briefing.
diablo_shareware: Blizzard's 1996 Diablo shareware: create a Warrior and walk into Tristram, the town above the dungeon. Characters are saved in this browser.
quake2_demo: id Software's Quake II demo, version 3.14: the 1997 shooter's first levels on its OpenGL renderer, plus network games over the emulator's virtual LAN.
quake3_demo: The Quake III Arena 1.11 demo from id Software: arena deathmatch on its OpenGL renderer, hosted or joined over the emulator's virtual LAN.
nfs2se_glide_demo: Electronic Arts' Need for Speed II Special Edition demo from 1997, racing on its 3dfx Glide renderer, which the emulator implements itself.
nfs3_glide_demo: The September 1998 Need for Speed III: Hot Pursuit demo, a Corvette on Rocky Pass, drawn by its 3dfx Glide renderer on the emulator's own Glide.
simcity2000_demo: Maxis's SimCity 2000 interactive demo for Windows 95: load the demo city or start a new one. As in the original demo, there is no saving and it ends after 30 minutes.
moorhuhn: Moorhuhn (Crazy Chicken), Phenomedia's 1999 promotional shooting game: 90 seconds to shoot as many chickens as you can across the countryside.
wep16_jezzball: JezzBall from Windows Entertainment Pack 4, the original 16-bit game: build walls to trap the bouncing atoms and fence off three quarters of the field.
heaven7: Heaven Seven, Exceed's winning 64K intro from Mekka & Symposium 2000. The site runs the final Windows build and starts it through its original setup dialog.
cashcow: Cashcow, Aardbei's Windows 64K intro from DreamHack 1999. It runs in the release's documented 512×384 windowed mode.
bakkslide7: Bakkslide 7, Hellcore & Omnicolour's Windows port of their first-place Takeover 1999 64K intro. The launcher selects its working 4:3 window and MMX transfer path.
ptct: Please the Cookie Thing, Aardbei's OpenGL 64K intro from Mekka & Symposium 2000. It runs through the original resolution chooser and Win9x-era fixed-function OpenGL path.
